Struck's (otherwise unpublished?) lexical analysis: 'He has proved that the vocabulary of Nagumi is made up of forty-two per cent. of words derived from primitive Bantu roots, while fifty-three per cent. are Sudanic'; 5-word Nagumi/Mboa/Jarawa table (blood kila, eye miso, head muro, stone tala, tooth maeno); then: 'As no phonetic treatment of the material which forms the basis for this chapter has at present been attempted, it is clear that the classification adopted can only be regarded as provisional'. sources.note: Read in full from page images (no text layer; 7 pages scanned for the extract). (1) The introduction pp. 47-50 is Struempell's own 'Zur Einfuehrung'; there are no Vorbemerkungen by Struck in this article. (2) The only remark on transcription is editor Meinhof's footnote 1 (pp. 47-48): spelling follows the Reichskolonialamt rules for geographical names (Routen-Aufnahmebuch 1911); it lists consonant letters that differ from Lepsius (w, ch, s, ss/sz, z = ts) and says consonant doubling is ambiguous between consonant length and short preceding vowel -- nothing on what the acute, macron or breve o…

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

Dieser Stamm soll suedlich Garua gesessen haben.' p. 134 conjectures that the people who left the Kalge mountains SW of Garua for Ngaundere before the Fulbe were the Nagumi. Ethnographic/migration notes only.
